blogs.title: Democratizing Large Language Model Finetuning: Introducing QLoRA
blogs.description: An overview of QLoRA, the new technique that shrinks memory requirements so you can finetune a 65‑billion‑parameter model on a single 48 GB GPU, while keeping the quality of full‑precision training. This post explains why this breakthrough matters for researchers, startups, and hobbyists.

blogs.title: Why 4‑Bit Is Enough: The Magic Behind NF4 Quantization
blogs.description: A deep‑dive into the 4‑bit NormalFloat (NF4) data type—how it leverages the normal distribution of weights to achieve information‑theoretic optimality, and why it outperforms traditional int4 and float4 quantization in practice.

blogs.title: Double Quantization & Paged Optimizers: Cutting Memory Spikes in Half
blogs.description: Explains two hidden heroes of QLoRA: Double Quantization, which compresses the quantization constants themselves, and Paged Optimizers, which use NVIDIA unified memory to avoid out‑of‑memory crashes during gradient checkpointing.

blogs.title: Guanaco vs. ChatGPT: How an Open‑Source Model Reached 99 % of ChatGPT’s Vicuna Score
blogs.description: Shows the experimental results that led to the Guanaco model family, detailing how a modest dataset and a single GPU can produce chatbot performance that rivals proprietary systems on the Vicuna benchmark.

blogs.title: Human Judges vs. GPT‑4: Evaluating Chatbot Quality at Scale
blogs.description: Discusses the novel evaluation pipeline used in the paper—pairwise Elo ratings from both human annotators and GPT‑4—highlighting strengths, biases, and why automated evaluation can be a cheap yet imperfect stand‑in for humans.

blogs.title: From GPU to Phone: Running Finetuned LLMs on Consumer Devices
blogs.description: Translates QLoRA’s memory savings into real‑world possibilities, such as finetuning a 7B model on a laptop or even an iPhone, enabling privacy‑preserving personal assistants without cloud reliance.

blogs.title: What QLoRA Reveals About LLM Training – Lessons Learned & Future Directions
blogs.description: Summarizes the paper’s key takeaways—data quality over quantity, mismatched benchmarks, limits of current PEFT methods—and outlines open research questions like 3‑bit quantization, alternative adapters, and more robust bias testing.
